short: The price where collective judgment converges
body: Fair Value represents the price at which most people agree an asset is worth. It is calculated by aggregating many independent price estimates and removing extreme outliers so that only the core consensus remains. Over time, fair value stabilizes as more participants contribute.

short: The current transaction price in the market
body: Market Price is the price at which an asset is currently being bought and sold. It may differ from fair value due to hype, panic, scarcity, promotions, or short-term supply and demand imbalances.

short: Value derived from fundamentals rather than opinion
body: Intrinsic Value is calculated based on expected future benefits such as cash flows, usefulness, or economic impact. It is often used by analysts to estimate what something should be worth regardless of market mood.

short: How reliable a valuation signal is
body: Confidence Score reflects how tightly user estimates cluster together. A high score means many people independently arrived at similar values. A low score means estimates are scattered, indicating uncertainty.

short: The middle value of all estimates
body: The median price is the middle number when all price estimates are sorted from lowest to highest. It is resistant to extreme outliers and is often a more reliable indicator than a simple average.

short: The average after removing extreme values
body: The trimmed mean removes the highest and lowest estimates before calculating the average. This prevents a few unrealistic guesses from distorting the crowd’s true opinion.

short: Value estimated by many independent users
body: Crowd valuation leverages the wisdom of many independent participants. When many people estimate the same item, their combined judgment is often more accurate than any single expert.

short: How markets determine the right price
body: Price discovery is the process through which buyers and sellers collectively determine what something is worth. On ValueVers, price discovery happens through user submissions rather than transactions.
